Market Desk · Daily Debrief · Tuesday, November 24, 2026

The AI bounce lasted one day. The money didn't leave; it moved to the Dow.

The S&P 500 slipped 0.5% to 7,201 after failing under the same ceiling it failed at on Monday, while the Nasdaq fell 1.5% and the chip ETF SMH 7.3%. The Dow rose 0.85% and closed over 50,000, and the equal-weight S&P rose 0.5%. Our read: Monday was short covering in AI; Tuesday was the bill, paid by the same names, while the rest of the market had a decent day. Dell beat and raised after the bell. PCE lands tomorrow at 8:30 a.m. with every idea on our list leaning the same way.

The miss first. Monday we said the rally "guaranteed nothing" and we were right about the index, but the move itself happened where we can't trade it: AMD, CRDO, SMH and NVDA fell 6–13% today and none of them has a contract near the money under $800 that passes our rules. The one idea that triggered, the GOOGL Dec 18 $270 put, came in intraday at $790 and closes at $732.50: GOOGL finished $279.05, only 45 cents under the $279.50 trigger line. The close agrees with the entry, barely.

What mattered today
  • The AI trade gave back half of Monday. SMH −7.3%, AMD −8.9% (a filing registers about 337M shares for possible resale), NVDA −5.9% to $155.38, CRDO −13.1%, Micron about −11%. HPE fell 16.3% after warning that memory and components stay scarce into the second half of 2028 and that AI margins narrow next year.
  • Rotation, not panic. The Dow +0.85% to 50,019, the equal-weight S&P +0.5%, small caps +0.5%, health care +3.0% (Sanofi agreed to buy Insmed for about $41B), staples +1.7%. Retailers ripped on results: Kohl's +19.5%, Dick's +14.6%, Dollar Tree +11.2%.
  • Consumers feel good. Conference Board confidence 103.3 vs about 92 expected (prior 91.9), the highest in nearly two years; 12-month inflation expectations eased to 5.7%.
  • Rates barely moved: the 10-year near 4.90–4.92%, a $70B 5-year auction cleared at 4.719%. A Dec 9 hike is priced near certain (about 95%).
  • Oil up, gold down: WTI about $81.46 (+1.6%) after Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they targeted a ship near Hormuz; gold about $3,552 (−2.7%); VIX 26.36.
  • Dell after the bell: revenue $54.9B vs about $49.2B expected, EPS $9.45 vs about $6.59, AI backlog $132.3B, full-year revenue guide raised to $202B. The stock fell 11.8% in the session and rose about 4% after hours.
  • Tomorrow: GDP, October PCE and jobless claims at 8:30 a.m., the Beige Book at 2:00 p.m. Thursday closed, Friday closes at 1:00 p.m.

The combination is quieter than the stock market. The dollar slipped 0.5% and the 10-year barely moved, yet gold fell 2.7% for a second big down day in a week; with a hike priced as a near certainty, gold is losing to real rates, not to the dollar. Oil firmed on the Hormuz headline but is still down about 18% in a month (USO), which keeps the inflation scare from getting worse before PCE. The VIX stayed above 26 on a day the S&P fell only 0.5%: options are still priced for big moves, which is why our put ideas need 2 to 1. Names hit: OXY and XOM got a small bid; JPM and BAC wait on a flat curve; GOOGL and IWM are the ideas most exposed to tomorrow's PCE.

What's going on

Four forces behind the day

1. The AI hardware trade has a supply problem, not a demand problem

What we see: SMH −7.3% the day after +15.0%. The biggest losers were the AI hardware and memory names: CRDO −13.1%, Micron about −11%, AMD −8.9%, INTC −8.1%, BE −7.0%, VRT −6.7%, NVDA −5.9%.

Why: HPE told investors on Monday night that memory and components could stay scarce through at least the second half of 2028 and guided its cloud and AI operating margin to about 14% next year from 18.4%; it fell 16.3%. That is a margin warning for everyone who builds AI servers, which is why DELL fell 11.8% before its own report. AMD added its own problem: a filing that registers about 337M shares for possible resale, with the sellers unnamed. We found no new information on Nvidia's SEC review or its 10-Q (due Dec 4); NVDA simply gave back a third of Monday's 31.5%.

Our read: demand is not the issue; Dell said tonight that demand is "further ahead of supply" in 2027 than in 2026. Cost and supply are. That makes the hardware names a margin story, and margin stories trade lower until the next print proves otherwise. How sure: medium. What would prove us wrong: SMH back over its 14-day ($463.87) on a close. Names: NVDA, AMD, INTC, SMH, CRDO, VRT, BE, DELL; GOOGL and AMZN as the AI backers.

2. Rotation: the rest of the market had a good day

What we see: the S&P 500 fell 0.5% but its equal-weight twin (RSP) rose 0.5%, the Dow rose 0.85% to a close over 50,000, small caps rose 0.5%. Health care +3.0%, staples +1.7%, real estate +1.3%; tech (XLK) −3.3%.

Why: money left the stocks that ran on Monday and went to cheaper, slower ones with good news of their own: Sanofi's $175-a-share cash deal for Insmed (+14.1%), and retail results strong enough to lift Kohl's 19.5%, Dick's 14.6% and Dollar Tree 11.2%. The consumer confidence beat backed the same trade.

Our read: this is healthier under the surface than the S&P print says, but it is not a turn. RSP's own 14-day crossed under its 30-day today, so even the broad market's direction just turned down. What would prove us wrong: RSP back over $217 (its 14/30-day) while SPX holds 7,138. Names: KO and AAPL (direction up, but calls stay blocked), JPM and BAC (the banks barely moved).

3. A strong consumer keeps the Fed hiking, and PCE is tomorrow

What we see: Conference Board confidence jumped 11.4 points to 103.3; the present-situation index rose to 132.8. A Dec 9 hike is priced near certain (CME FedWatch about 95%), with a January follow-up about 59% priced (Trading Economics). The 10-year held near 4.90–4.92%.

Why it matters: a hiking Fed with a confident consumer has no reason to stop. New York Fed President Williams said Monday he "would not exclude… moving at consecutive meetings." Tomorrow's core PCE is expected at +0.3% for October (about 3.2% from a year ago), alongside the GDP revision (consensus 3.5%) and claims (about 201K).

What it means for the ideas: every active idea is a put (GOOGL, IWM, BAC, JPM, AMZN, plus the older PLTR, BA and OXY ideas). A soft PCE is the one print that could squeeze all of them at once; see the red line in the plays section. A hot one helps the IWM and bank puts most. What would prove us wrong: core PCE at +0.1% and hike odds for January falling under 40%.

4. Dell: beat, raise, and a margin step-down

Numbers vs consensus: revenue $54.9B (+103%) vs about $49.2B; non-GAAP EPS $9.45 vs about $6.59; AI-optimized server revenue $22.0B (+291%), AI orders $60.2B, record AI backlog $132.3B.

Guidance and risk: fiscal 2027 revenue raised to $202B from $192B (consensus about $193.5B), EPS to $29.68 from $25.50; Q4 revenue guide $56.25B. The catch: the CFO said infrastructure margins "will sequentially moderate" (about 17% to just under 15%), inventory has nearly tripled since January to $29.4B, and memory prices are not expected to fall. New $25B buyback.

Chart and trade verdict: DELL closed $295.28, 41 cents over the 61.8% retracement of its Jan → Sep run ($294.87), and traded about $307.7 after hours. The weekly options priced a move of about ±$39.50 (13.4%); the after-hours move is about a third of that, so earnings buyers mostly lost. No trade: IV is near 190% tonight and every Dec contract near the money costs well over $800. Full breakdown on Market Desk: Dell Q3 FY2027 breakdown.

Down most: CRDO −13.1%, DELL −11.8%, AMD −8.9%, INTC −8.1%, SMH −7.3%, BE −7.0%, VRT −6.7%, ANT −6.5%, NVDA −5.9%, SPCX −5.7%. Up most: KO +1.8%, AAPL +1.4%, OXY +1.3%, PLTR +1.1%.

Read it top to bottom and it's a two-market day: KO, Apple, the banks and oil green; every AI hardware name red. Nine of the ten worst names on the list sit in the AI trade; the tenth is SpaceX.

Lesson of the day

A peer's earnings can move your stock before its own report does

DELL lost 11.8% today because of HPE, not because of Dell. HPE reported Monday night and warned that memory and components stay scarce into late 2028 and that AI server margins shrink next year. Dell sells the same kind of server to the same customers, so investors priced HPE's warning into Dell a day early: $39.63 a share, before Dell said a word.

Then Dell's own numbers moved it the other way, about +$12.4 after hours. Two reports, two moves, in opposite directions inside 24 hours.

Why this matters for an options buyer: the weekly DELL straddle at $295 cost about $39.50 this afternoon, a bet on a 13.4% move. After hours the stock moved about 4%. Implied volatility near 190% will collapse tomorrow, and a call buyer who was right on direction still loses most of the premium. That is the earnings crush, and the read-through day (HPE's report) is when the crush got priced in.

The rule we already use: every idea carries an "event risk" line, and a peer's report counts. Before Dell's report, the event line for any AI-server idea should have named HPE on Monday night. Tonight the same logic says: any NVDA idea names the 10-Q (Dec 4); any IWM or bank idea names PCE tomorrow at 8:30.

Practice: for each idea in the plays section, write down the one report, peer or data release that could move it before our first target. If you can't name one, look harder.

AMD: a wick under the 1.382, and why RSI under 40 isn't a buy here

Key levels (the desk's 3-day extension): 2.0 $558.82 · 1.618 $464.60 · 1.382 $406.39 (today's lesson) · 0.786 $259.39.

The level. The desk's 3-day extension on AMD uses A $264.64, B $511.29, C $65.52, so B − A = $246.65. The 1.382 = 65.52 + 1.382 × 246.65 = $406.39. The 1.618 above it = $464.60 (broke Nov 20); the 0.786 below = $259.39.

What price did. AMD traded $396.01 today, $10.38 (2.6%) under the 1.382, and closed $413.27. The drawing is on 3-day candles, and the Nov 20–24 candle closed back over the line: a wick on its own timeframe, the second time this line has turned price (Nov 6 low $402.10).

Fibs plus RSI (concept 18). RSI is 38.7 and the 50-day ($550.48) is still over the 200-day ($432.00), so the old tested edge (uptrend + RSI under 40) would call this a buy. It isn't: price is under the 50-day and under a broken 1.618, and the 14-day crossed under the 30-day on Oct 22. RSI under 40 counts only when price is holding over its key level and the 50-day. Here it is weakness, not cheapness.

Trade: none. Calls are blocked and no AMD contract near the money costs under $800. A 3-day close under $406.39 opens the 0.786 ($259.39); a 3-day close back over $464.60 is the first sign of repair.
